WIC27A-01.note: Same families at the counters and no building newer than 1951 point to a town frozen in place. 'Drained' fits the traffic loss but not the persistence; 'engulfed' is the opposite of a bypass.

WIC27A-02.note: Papers lost advertisers, pages, bureaus and wire service, so they were crippled; radio still read their stories, which rules out dethroned. The single shared bulletin gives 'homogenized' some support, though the local content cuts against it.

WIC27A-03.note: Coal stockpile and coal-burning ships calling while sailing ships pass make it a coaling depot; 'gateway' and 'haven' fit the strait loosely.

WIC27A-04.note: Founders meeting, couriers dispatched, files kept: headquarters. 'Hub' covers the couriers and letters and is close; 'embassy' is tempting from the foreign-capital setting.

WIC27A-05.note: Adult salmon rest in the pool and spawn miles upstream later, so it is a stopover; the log lies parallel to the current (not a route), seedlings die (not garden), spawning is elsewhere (not hatchery).

WIC27A-06.note: The ruling let the union stand and employers kept paying scale (not disbanded, not defanged); barring new members guaranteed its slow death.

WIC27A-07.note: Same length rules out distilled; the desert setting is kept, ruling out domesticated; every reworking sharpens the structure, so honed.

WIC27A-08.note: One family owns it, tenants harvest and dates go to the family's own warehouses, caravans water free: a private estate, not a trading place.

WIC27B-01.note: Both ends logged the same night (no stopover, not inn or lair) and vole counts unchanged (not larder): the hedge is a travel route.

WIC27B-02.note: Sand filled the hollows and fields were plowed straight for the first time; wheat no thicker in the hollows rules out nourished.

WIC27B-03.note: Walled ledge of ochre-dusted human bones with the living camps by the river makes it a burial place; the burial sentence alone decides.

WIC27B-04.note: Shipyard payments load by load from an oak estate, then stump-pulling: the woods were cut. Unchanged hands' wages rule out liquidated or leased.

WIC27B-05.note: Behavior unchanged (not manipulated), eggs weekly (not neutered), equal disease losses (not immunized); the worm drains growth and energy. 'Manipulated' is the strong textbook distractor.

WIC27B-06.note: Uniform yearly layers that ignore weather served as the exact year-count others dated against: a timekeeper. 'Ledger' can be read as a record of years, though the lake records no weather.

WIC27B-07.note: Interchangeable parts and designs worked from bought machines show copying; 'leapfrogged' fits the sales lead but not the method.

WIC27B-08.note: Twelve owners' marks and a shed shared by a crew of twelve make it a pooled fund; coins from many trading ports undercut loot.

WIC27C-01.note: Outside strains grown beside local wheat and reported before adoption: a testing ground. The forty-year run rules out stopgap; the strains came from elsewhere, so not wellspring.

WIC27C-02.note: Merchants and boats moved to the village while fish still reached the same shops: the market was relocated, not choked.

WIC27C-03.note: Bare grooved rock and debris offshore mean swept clean; unchanged tide mark and stream course rule out submerged and tilted, bare rock rules out smothered.

WIC27C-04.note: Water leaks away through the floor and the river leaves half as wide; shallowness means no cooling (not thermostat). The lake loses water: a sink.

WIC27C-05.note: Paint moved off the oak onto canvas; still smoke-browned rules out scrubbed and uncovered.

WIC27C-06.note: It flings bodies out and some inward across the rocky planets (not umbrella); it halves the belt (not shepherd, not tether).

WIC27C-07.note: Three-minute sides cut twenty-verse ballads to five or six; recorded as found (not smoothed), sold locally (not transplanted). 'Stripped' is a slightly loose fit for truncated.

WIC27C-08.note: It stored whole imported cars and parts and dispatched them on order; selling there since 1930 rules out toehold.

WIC27D-01.note: Dry shore-to-island at low tide plus sheep on the island pasture: a walkway. The fleet sails over it anywhere and winters on the beach, so not barricade, chokepoint or breakwater.

WIC27D-02.note: Cobbles exposed on the crest and less erosion afterward; the road, hook and boathouses are unchanged, ruling out cleaved, blunted and broadened.

WIC27D-03.note: Spring water piped to fountains on both sides while the wells are brackish: a drinking-water supply. 'Artery' is a defensible metaphor for a vital supply line; fenced banks rule out commons.

WIC27D-04.note: Grain sold to the highest bidder even in famine (not backstop) and no hearth tax except when the river closed: the granary was the revenue source.

WIC27D-05.note: Lit, stocked galleries the square emptied into at sirens: an air-raid shelter. The 1940-44 sentence alone decides.

WIC27D-06.note: Shallows from both banks and carts reaching the far town via the island: a ford. Burned barns and flood lines rule out citadel and ark.

WIC27D-07.note: Still air (upright flame) rules out chimney and bellows; the basin the village draws from makes it a water store.

WIC27D-08.note: Faint brushwork and rims no longer translucent mean the glaze went opaque; smooth surface and stain-free wash rule out blistered and cracked; whiter ground rules out blackened.

WIC27E-01.note: Clear water draining through a salt crust and restoring yields means the salt was washed out; grazing no better rules out replenished.

WIC27E-02.note: Same festival week, taller gate, city tolls halved; monks from a different order rule out offshoot, wooden and smaller rules out replica.

WIC27E-03.note: Dark water and cod hiding under the ice from sight-hunting birds: cover overhead. Nothing grows there, so not pantry.

WIC27E-04.note: Flow held (mill at normal speed), so not parched or pinched; trout died only in the shallow treeless miles and lived by the cold springs: heat.

WIC27E-05.note: Empty houses filled, families stayed, school reopened; 'reoriented' to farming is the only near-miss. 'Ruined' and 'overran' go against the passage's whole tone.

WIC27E-06.note: Surface craters in scattered pockets with forest between: pitted, not riddled (worked in daylight, no tunnels). The hatchery and the mountain still shading the town rule out poisoned and razed.

WIC27E-07.note: Rate swung with alternating parties and ended where it started: oscillation, not one-way ratchet. Rises in record-price years rule out regulator.

WIC27E-08.note: Seals on the doors, banned authors still shelved and dust everywhere: locked up and unused, not purged, plundered or pulped.
